773	def commit(paths: dict[str, str], request: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, str]:
774	    """Run one replayable commit across storage, audit, receipt and checkpoint.
775	
776	    ``paths`` must contain exactly the str keys ``checkpoint``, ``state``,
777	    ``audit`` and ``receipt``.  ``request`` must contain exactly the keys
778	    ``id`` (same format as :func:`checkpoint`), ``state`` (a state obeying
779	    the :mod:`~offline_coordination.merge` state contract) and ``event``
780	    (an event obeying the :mod:`~offline_coordination.audit` event
781	    contract).
782	
783	    The state digest is the lowercase-hex SHA-256 of the complete
784	    canonical state bytes (including the trailing ``\\n``) that
785	    :mod:`~offline_coordination.storage` persists; the audit digest is
786	    the hash of the single audit record appended for this commit.  A
787	    first commit saves the state, appends exactly one audit event, binds
788	    a receipt carrying the id and both digests, and advances the
789	    checkpoint through ``prepared``, ``state``, ``audit`` and
790	    ``committed`` in that order.
791	
792	    Replaying the same arguments -- or re-entering after an interruption
793	    -- resumes at the recorded stage and performs each remaining side
794	    effect at most once, so the result is identical and no effect is
795	    duplicated.  Every artifact is reconciled against the checkpoint
796	    stage before any file is touched: a digest conflict, or a stage
797	    whose state file, audit record or receipt is missing, extra or
798	    mismatched, raises :class:`ValueError` and leaves the files
799	    unchanged.
800	
801	    On success a brand-new dict is returned with the key order
802	    ``audit``, ``id``, ``stage``, ``state`` and ``stage`` equal to
803	    ``committed``.  Type violations raise :class:`TypeError`; bad key
804	    sets, formats, state/event values, digest conflicts and stage/
805	    artifact mismatches raise :class:`ValueError`;
806	    :class:`CorruptStateError`, :class:`CorruptAuditError`,
807	    :class:`CorruptReceiptError`, :class:`CorruptTransactionError` and
808	    :class:`OSError` propagate unchanged.
809	    """
810	    (
811	        path_map,
812	        checkpoint_id,
813	        state,
814	        event,
815	        payload,
816	    ) = _validated_commit_inputs(paths, request)
817	    checkpoint_path = path_map[_CHECKPOINT]
818	    state_path = path_map[STATE]
819	    audit_path = path_map[AUDIT]
820	    receipt_path = path_map[_RECEIPT]
821	
822	    state_digest = hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest()
823	
824	    # Read every artifact up front.  All reconciliation below happens
825	    # before any mutation, so a rejected commit changes nothing.
826	    audit_records = _audit._read_all_records(audit_path)
827	    planned_audit_digest = _planned_audit_digest(audit_records, event)
828	    bound_receipt = _receipt.get(receipt_path, checkpoint_id)
829	    records = _read_index(checkpoint_path)
830	    existing = next(
831	        (record for record in records if record[ID] == checkpoint_id), None
832	    )
833	    state_on_disk = _read_state_bytes(state_path)
834	    # When a state file exists but neither the main file nor the backup
835	    # holds a valid state the situation is unrecoverable, not a digest
836	    # conflict: CorruptStateError propagates before any reconciliation.
837	    _assert_state_loadable(state_path)
838	
839	    need_save = False
840	    need_append = False
841	    need_receipt = False
842	
843	    if existing is None:
844	        # An id absent from the checkpoint index cannot have produced any
845	        # artifact of its own yet; a receipt bound under it is a conflict.
846	        if bound_receipt is not None:
847	            raise ValueError(
848	                f"receipt id {checkpoint_id!r} is already bound but no "
849	                "checkpoint exists for it"
850	            )
851	        audit_digest = planned_audit_digest
852	        stage = PREPARED
853	        # The state save is the first artifact effect; it is pending
854	        # unless the main file already holds the committed bytes.
855	        need_save = state_on_disk != payload
856	        need_append = True
857	        need_receipt = True
858	    else:
859	        if existing[STATE] != state_digest:
860	            raise ValueError(
861	                f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} is already bound to a "
862	                "different state digest"
863	            )
864	        audit_digest = existing[AUDIT]
865	        stage = existing[STAGE]
866	        audit_record = next(
867	            (item for item in audit_records
868	             if item[_audit.HASH] == audit_digest),
869	            None,
870	        )
871	
872	        if stage == PREPARED:
873	            # The event has not been appended yet, so its record hash must
874	            # still be derivable from the current log tail.
875	            if audit_digest != planned_audit_digest:
876	                raise ValueError(
877	                    f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} is already bound to a "
878	                    "different audit digest"
879	                )
880	            if audit_record is not None:
881	                raise ValueError(
882	                    f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} is at stage 'prepared' "
883	                    "but its audit record is already present"
884	                )
885	            if bound_receipt is not None:
886	                raise ValueError(
887	                    f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} is at stage 'prepared' "
888	                    "but a receipt is already bound"
889	                )
890	            # The save is pending unless the main file already holds the
891	            # committed bytes; save_state itself rotates any prior state.
892	            need_save = state_on_disk != payload
893	            need_append = True
894	            need_receipt = True
895	        elif stage == STAGE_STATE:
896	            if state_on_disk != payload:
897	                raise ValueError(
898	                    f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} is past stage "
899	                    "'prepared' but its state file is missing or mismatched"
900	                )
901	            if bound_receipt is not None:
902	                raise ValueError(
903	                    f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} is at stage 'state' but "
904	                    "a receipt is already bound"
905	                )
906	            if audit_record is None:
907	                # The append may still be pending; the log tail must still
908	                # derive the bound record for this event.
909	                if audit_digest != planned_audit_digest:
910	                    raise ValueError(
911	                        f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} is at stage 'state' "
912	                        "but its audit record is missing"
913	                    )
914	                need_append = True
915	            elif not _event_matches(audit_record, event):
916	                raise ValueError(
917	                    f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} audit record does not "
918	                    "match its committed event"
919	                )
920	            need_receipt = True
921	        elif stage == STAGE_AUDIT:
922	            if state_on_disk != payload:
923	                raise ValueError(
924	                    f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} is past stage "
925	                    "'prepared' but its state file is missing or mismatched"
926	                )
927	            if audit_record is None:
928	                raise ValueError(
929	                    f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} is past stage 'state' "
930	                    "but its audit record is missing"
931	                )
932	            if not _event_matches(audit_record, event):
933	                raise ValueError(
934	                    f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} audit record does not "
935	                    "match its committed event"
936	                )
937	            if bound_receipt is None:
938	                need_receipt = True
939	            elif (
940	                bound_receipt[STATE] != state_digest
941	                or bound_receipt[AUDIT] != audit_digest
942	            ):
943	                raise ValueError(
944	                    f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} receipt is bound to "
945	                    "different state or audit digests"
946	                )
947	        else:  # COMMITTED
948	            if state_on_disk != payload:
949	                raise ValueError(
950	                    f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} is past stage "
951	                    "'prepared' but its state file is missing or mismatched"
952	                )
953	            if audit_record is None:
954	                raise ValueError(
955	                    f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} is past stage 'state' "
956	                    "but its audit record is missing"
957	                )
958	            if not _event_matches(audit_record, event):
959	                raise ValueError(
960	                    f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} audit record does not "
961	                    "match its committed event"
962	                )
963	            if bound_receipt is None:
964	                raise ValueError(
965	                    f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} is committed but its "
966	                    "receipt is missing"
967	                )
968	            if (
969	                bound_receipt[STATE] != state_digest
970	                or bound_receipt[AUDIT] != audit_digest
971	            ):
972	                raise ValueError(
973	                    f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} receipt is bound to "
974	                    "different state or audit digests"
975	                )
976	
977	    # Reconciliation succeeded; perform each remaining effect at most
978	    # once and advance the checkpoint after every durable step.
979	    if existing is None:
980	        records = _advance(
981	            checkpoint_path, records, checkpoint_id,
982	            state_digest, audit_digest, PREPARED,
983	        )
984	
985	    if stage == PREPARED:

"""Replayable commit checkpoints for offline coordination.

A checkpoint names an ``id``, the two 64-char lowercase hex digests of the
state and audit bytes it binds, and the ``stage`` the commit has reached.
Stages advance in the fixed order::

    prepared -> state -> audit -> committed

Checkpoints are kept in an index stored as UTF-8 compact JSON::

    {"items":[{"audit":...,"id":...,"stage":...,"state":...},...],"version":1}\\n

The top-level keys are fixed in the order ``items`` then ``version`` and
``version`` is always the integer 1.  ``items`` is an array of records
sorted ascending by ``id`` (ids are unique); each record carries the str
keys ``audit``, ``id``, ``stage`` and ``state`` in that order.  Non-ASCII
characters are preserved unescaped and the file ends with exactly one
``\\n``.

A missing index file stands for an empty index.  An existing file is
corrupt unless it is one compact UTF-8 JSON encoding of a valid index:
no stray whitespace or non-canonical escapes and exactly one trailing
``\\n``.  The object *key order* carries no meaning, however, so an
otherwise identical compact encoding with the top-level or record keys
permuted is accepted as equivalent; files written by this module always
use the canonical key order described above.

A brand-new id may only be recorded at the ``prepared`` stage.  Replaying
the same id with identical digests at the same stage is idempotent and
leaves the file bytes untouched; the stage may then advance one step at a
time, each advance replacing the file atomically.  Changed digests, a
stage regression or a skipped stage are rejected and never touch the file.

:func:`resume` drives a single recovery step.  Its request carries only
the ``id``, ``state`` and ``audit`` digests and ``observed`` names the
stage the caller believes it has reached (``None`` for a fresh resume).
A new id is only accepted with ``observed=None`` and starts at
``prepared``.  For an existing id with identical digests, ``observed``
of ``None`` or the current stage only queries the index (leaving the
file bytes untouched), while the adjacent next stage advances it once;
a regression, a skipped stage or an illegal value is rejected without
touching the file.  The return value names the next action for the
processed stage: ``persist_state`` after ``prepared``,
``append_audit`` after ``state``, ``bind_receipt`` after ``audit`` and
``done`` after ``committed``.

:func:`commit` drives a whole commit to completion.  Its ``paths`` map
names the ``checkpoint``, ``state``, ``audit`` and ``receipt`` files and
its request carries the ``id``, the full merge ``state`` and one audit
``event``.  The state digest is the SHA-256 of the canonical state bytes
storage writes; the audit digest is the hash of the one appended audit
record.  A first commit persists the state, appends exactly one event,
binds a receipt for the id and both digests, and advances the checkpoint
through the stages in order.  Replaying the same call -- after an
interruption or once committed -- deterministically resumes at the
recorded stage and performs every remaining side effect at most once,
returning the same ``audit``, ``id``, ``stage`` (``committed``) and
``state`` dict.  A digest conflict, or a checkpoint stage whose
artifacts do not match it, raises :class:`ValueError` and leaves the
files unchanged.

:func:`inspect` is a strictly read-only counterpart taking only the
``paths`` map.  A missing checkpoint index yields an empty list; every
existing checkpoint is reported with its ``audit``, ``id``, ``stage``
and ``state`` values plus a ``status`` of ``recoverable``,
``committed`` or ``conflict`` derived from the state bytes, the audit
chain and any bound receipt.  Neither :func:`inspect` nor
:func:`commit` ever treats an existing-but-unreadable state as a mere
conflict: when at least one of the main and backup state files exists
but neither holds a valid state, :class:`CorruptStateError` propagates.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
from typing import Any

from . import audit as _audit
from . import receipt as _receipt
from . import storage as _storage

AUDIT = "audit"
ID = "id"
STAGE = "stage"
STATE = "state"
STATUS = "status"

ITEMS = "items"
VERSION = "version"

PREPARED = "prepared"
STAGE_STATE = "state"
STAGE_AUDIT = "audit"
COMMITTED = "committed"

_REQUEST_KEYS = (ID, STATE, AUDIT, STAGE)
_RESUME_KEYS = (ID, STATE, AUDIT)
_COMMIT_KEYS = (ID, STATE, "event")
_PATH_KEYS = ("checkpoint", STATE, AUDIT, "receipt")
_RECORD_KEYS = (AUDIT, ID, STAGE, STATE)
_INDEX_KEYS = (ITEMS, VERSION)
_INDEX_VERSION = 1

_EVENT = "event"
_CHECKPOINT = "checkpoint"
_RECEIPT = "receipt"

_STAGES = (PREPARED, STAGE_STATE, STAGE_AUDIT, COMMITTED)
_STAGE_RANK = {stage: rank for rank, stage in enumerate(_STAGES)}

# Statuses reported by inspect for a checkpoint against its artifacts.
RECOVERABLE = "recoverable"
CONFLICT = "conflict"

# Action performed once the checkpoint for a stage has been durably
# recorded: persist state after prepared, append the audit entry after
# state, bind the receipt after audit, and nothing after committed.
_NEXT_ACTIONS = {
    PREPARED: "persist_state",
    STAGE_STATE: "append_audit",
    STAGE_AUDIT: "bind_receipt",
    COMMITTED: "done",
}

_ID_RE = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}\Z")
_DIGEST_RE = re.compile(r"[0-9a-f]{64}\Z")


class CorruptTransactionError(ValueError):
    """The checkpoint index exists but its bytes are not a valid index."""


def _is_digest(value: Any) -> bool:
    return isinstance(value, str) and _DIGEST_RE.fullmatch(value) is not None


def _validated_request(request: Any) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Validate one checkpoint request and return a fresh dict in record order."""
    if not isinstance(request, dict):
        raise TypeError("request must be a dict")
    if set(request.keys()) != set(_REQUEST_KEYS):
        raise ValueError(
            "request must contain exactly the keys 'id', 'state', 'audit' "
            "and 'stage'"
        )
    for key in _REQUEST_KEYS:
        if not isinstance(request[key], str):
            raise TypeError(f"request {key} must be a str")
    checkpoint_id = request[ID]
    if _ID_RE.fullmatch(checkpoint_id) is None:
        raise ValueError("request id must match [A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}")
    if not _is_digest(request[STATE]):
        raise ValueError("request state must be 64 lowercase hex characters")
    if not _is_digest(request[AUDIT]):
        raise ValueError("request audit must be 64 lowercase hex characters")
    stage = request[STAGE]
    if stage not in _STAGE_RANK:
        raise ValueError(
            "request stage must be one of 'prepared', 'state', 'audit' or "
            "'committed'"
        )
    return {
        AUDIT: request[AUDIT],
        ID: checkpoint_id,
        STAGE: stage,
        STATE: request[STATE],
    }


def _validated_resume_request(request: Any) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Validate one resume request and return a fresh dict in record order."""
    if not isinstance(request, dict):
        raise TypeError("request must be a dict")
    if set(request.keys()) != set(_RESUME_KEYS):
        raise ValueError(
            "request must contain exactly the keys 'id', 'state' and 'audit'"
        )
    for key in _RESUME_KEYS:
        if not isinstance(request[key], str):
            raise TypeError(f"request {key} must be a str")
    checkpoint_id = request[ID]
    if _ID_RE.fullmatch(checkpoint_id) is None:
        raise ValueError("request id must match [A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}")
    if not _is_digest(request[STATE]):
        raise ValueError("request state must be 64 lowercase hex characters")
    if not _is_digest(request[AUDIT]):
        raise ValueError("request audit must be 64 lowercase hex characters")
    return {
        AUDIT: request[AUDIT],
        ID: checkpoint_id,
        STATE: request[STATE],
    }


def _serialize_index(records: list[dict[str, str]]) -> bytes:
    ordered = [
        {AUDIT: record[AUDIT], ID: record[ID], STAGE: record[STAGE],
         STATE: record[STATE]}
        for record in records
    ]
    index = {ITEMS: ordered, VERSION: _INDEX_VERSION}
    text = json.dumps(index, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":")) + "\n"
    return text.encode("utf-8")


def _parse_index(raw: bytes) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    """Validate every byte of a checkpoint index and return its records.

    Raises :class:`CorruptTransactionError` for any UTF-8/JSON failure,
    non-canonical byte encoding, wrong key set, bad version, duplicate or
    unsorted ids, or a field that is not a well-formed str.  The order of
    object keys does not matter: a compact encoding whose only difference
    from the canonical form is key permutation is an equivalent index.
    """
    if raw == b"":
        raise CorruptTransactionError("checkpoint index is empty")
    try:
        text = raw.decode("utf-8")
    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
        raise CorruptTransactionError("checkpoint index is not valid UTF-8") from exc
    try:
        data = json.loads(text)
    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
        raise CorruptTransactionError("checkpoint index is not valid JSON") from exc

    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        raise CorruptTransactionError("checkpoint index must be a JSON object")
    if set(data.keys()) != set(_INDEX_KEYS):
        raise CorruptTransactionError(
            "checkpoint index must contain exactly the keys 'items' and 'version'"
        )
    version = data[VERSION]
    # bool is a subclass of int; the version must be a genuine integer.
    if isinstance(version, bool) or not isinstance(version, int) or version != 1:
        raise CorruptTransactionError("checkpoint index version must be the integer 1")
    raw_items = data[ITEMS]
    if not isinstance(raw_items, list):
        raise CorruptTransactionError("checkpoint index items must be an array")

    records: list[dict[str, str]] = []
    for position, item in enumerate(raw_items):
        where = f"checkpoint index item {position}"
        if not isinstance(item, dict):
            raise CorruptTransactionError(f"{where} must be a JSON object")
        if set(item.keys()) != set(_RECORD_KEYS):
            raise CorruptTransactionError(
                f"{where} must contain exactly the keys 'audit', 'id', 'stage' "
                "and 'state'"
            )
        audit_digest = item[AUDIT]
        record_id = item[ID]
        stage = item[STAGE]
        state_digest = item[STATE]
        if not isinstance(record_id, str) or _ID_RE.fullmatch(record_id) is None:
            raise CorruptTransactionError(f"{where} has an invalid id")
        if not isinstance(stage, str) or stage not in _STAGE_RANK:
            raise CorruptTransactionError(f"{where} has an invalid stage")
        if not isinstance(state_digest, str) or not _is_digest(state_digest):
            raise CorruptTransactionError(
                f"{where} state must be 64 lowercase hex characters"
            )
        if not isinstance(audit_digest, str) or not _is_digest(audit_digest):
            raise CorruptTransactionError(
                f"{where} audit must be 64 lowercase hex characters"
            )
        records.append(
            {AUDIT: audit_digest, ID: record_id, STAGE: stage, STATE: state_digest}
        )

    ids = [record[ID] for record in records]
    if any(left >= right for left, right in zip(ids, ids[1:])):
        raise CorruptTransactionError(
            "checkpoint index ids must be unique and sorted ascending"
        )

    # Reject stray whitespace, non-canonical escapes, duplicate keys and
    # any encoding that is not a single compact form of the validated
    # structure.  Re-serialising the parsed object while preserving its
    # parsed key order tolerates permuted object keys (a semantically
    # equivalent compact index) while still rejecting every other
    # byte-level deviation; writes always use the canonical key order of
    # _serialize_index.
    if not raw.endswith(b"\n") or raw.endswith(b"\n\n"):
        raise CorruptTransactionError(
            "checkpoint index must end with exactly one newline"
        )
    compact = json.dumps(data, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))
    if compact != text[:-1]:
        raise CorruptTransactionError("checkpoint index is not canonically encoded")
    return records


def _read_index(path: str) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    try:
        with open(path, "rb") as handle:
            raw = handle.read()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return []
    return _parse_index(raw)


def _atomic_write(path: str, payload: bytes) -> None:
    tmp_path = path + ".tmp"
    with open(tmp_path, "wb") as handle:
        handle.write(payload)
        handle.flush()
        os.fsync(handle.fileno())
    try:
        os.replace(tmp_path, path)
    except BaseException:
        try:
            os.unlink(tmp_path)
        except OSError:
            pass
        raise
    fd = os.open(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path)), os.O_RDONLY)
    try:
        os.fsync(fd)
    finally:
        os.close(fd)


def _apply(
    path: str, records: list[dict[str, str]], record: dict[str, str]
) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    """Apply ``record`` to ``records`` and return the resulting record list."""
    for position, existing in enumerate(records):
        if existing[ID] != record[ID]:
            continue
        if (
            existing[STATE] != record[STATE]
            or existing[AUDIT] != record[AUDIT]
        ):
            raise ValueError(
                f"checkpoint id {record[ID]!r} is already bound to different "
                "state or audit digests"
            )
        old_rank = _STAGE_RANK[existing[STAGE]]
        new_rank = _STAGE_RANK[record[STAGE]]
        if new_rank == old_rank:
            # Idempotent replay: no filesystem change.
            return records
        if new_rank < old_rank:
            raise ValueError(
                f"checkpoint id {record[ID]!r} cannot regress from stage "
                f"{existing[STAGE]!r} to {record[STAGE]!r}"
            )
        if new_rank > old_rank + 1:
            raise ValueError(
                f"checkpoint id {record[ID]!r} cannot skip from stage "
                f"{existing[STAGE]!r} to {record[STAGE]!r}"
            )
        updated = list(records)
        updated[position] = record
        _atomic_write(path, _serialize_index(updated))
        return updated

    if record[STAGE] != PREPARED:
        raise ValueError("a new checkpoint id must start at the 'prepared' stage")
    updated = sorted(records + [record], key=lambda entry: entry[ID])
    _atomic_write(path, _serialize_index(updated))
    return updated


def checkpoint(
    path: str, request: dict[str, str] | None = None
) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    """Record or query a replayable commit checkpoint at ``path``.

    With ``request=None`` this is a pure query returning every checkpoint.
    Otherwise ``request`` must contain exactly the str keys ``id``,
    ``state``, ``audit`` and ``stage``: ``id`` matches
    ``[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}``, ``state`` and ``audit`` are 64 lowercase hex
    characters, and ``stage`` is one of ``prepared``, ``state``, ``audit``
    or ``committed``.

    A new id is inserted at ``prepared``; an existing id with identical
    digests replays idempotently at the same stage or advances one adjacent
    stage.  Changed digests, a stage regression or a skipped stage raise
    :class:`ValueError` and leave the file unchanged.  In every case a
    brand-new list sorted ascending by ``id`` is returned, each element a
    fresh dict with the key order ``audit``, ``id``, ``stage``, ``state``.

    Type violations raise :class:`TypeError`; a bad key set, field format
    or stage migration raises :class:`ValueError`; a corrupt index raises
    :class:`CorruptTransactionError`; other filesystem errors propagate as
    :class:`OSError`.
    """
    if not isinstance(path, str):
        raise TypeError("path must be a str")

    record = _validated_request(request) if request is not None else None
    records = _read_index(path)
    if record is not None:
        records = _apply(path, records, record)

    return [
        {
            AUDIT: record[AUDIT],
            ID: record[ID],
            STAGE: record[STAGE],
            STATE: record[STATE],
        }
        for record in records
    ]


def resume(
    path: str, request: dict[str, str], observed: str | None = None
) -> str:
    """Recover one commit step at ``path`` and return the next action.

    ``request`` must contain exactly the str keys ``id``, ``state`` and
    ``audit`` in the same format as the matching :func:`checkpoint`
    fields.  ``observed`` must be ``None`` or one of the stages
    ``prepared``, ``state``, ``audit`` or ``committed``; it names the
    stage the caller has observed for the id.

    A new id is only accepted with ``observed=None`` and is recorded at
    the ``prepared`` stage.  An existing id must be bound to the same
    ``state`` and ``audit`` digests; with ``observed=None`` or the
    current stage the call is a pure query and leaves the file bytes
    untouched, while ``observed`` naming the adjacent next stage
    advances the checkpoint exactly once.  A stage regression, a skipped
    stage or an illegal ``observed`` value raise :class:`ValueError` and
    leave the file unchanged.

    The return value is the next action for the processed stage:
    ``persist_state`` for ``prepared``, ``append_audit`` for ``state``,
    ``bind_receipt`` for ``audit`` and ``done`` for ``committed``.

    A non-str ``observed`` other than ``None`` raises :class:`TypeError`;
    the remaining type and value rules, :class:`CorruptTransactionError`
    and :class:`OSError` propagation match :func:`checkpoint`.
    """
    if not isinstance(path, str):
        raise TypeError("path must be a str")

    requested = _validated_resume_request(request)
    if observed is not None:
        if not isinstance(observed, str):
            raise TypeError(
                "observed must be None or one of 'prepared', 'state', "
                "'audit' or 'committed'"
            )
        if observed not in _STAGE_RANK:
            raise ValueError(
                "observed must be None or one of 'prepared', 'state', "
                "'audit' or 'committed'"
            )

    records = _read_index(path)
    existing = next(
        (record for record in records if record[ID] == requested[ID]), None
    )

    if existing is None:
        if observed is not None:
            raise ValueError(
                f"checkpoint id {requested[ID]!r} is new and may only be "
                "resumed with observed=None"
            )
        record = {
            AUDIT: requested[AUDIT],
            ID: requested[ID],
            STAGE: PREPARED,
            STATE: requested[STATE],
        }
        _apply(path, records, record)
        return _NEXT_ACTIONS[PREPARED]

    if (
        existing[STATE] != requested[STATE]
        or existing[AUDIT] != requested[AUDIT]
    ):
        raise ValueError(
            f"checkpoint id {requested[ID]!r} is already bound to different "
            "state or audit digests"
        )

    current_stage = existing[STAGE]
    if observed is None or observed == current_stage:
        # Pure query: no filesystem change.
        processed_stage = current_stage
    else:
        current_rank = _STAGE_RANK[current_stage]
        observed_rank = _STAGE_RANK[observed]
        if observed_rank < current_rank:
            raise ValueError(
                f"checkpoint id {requested[ID]!r} cannot regress from stage "
                f"{current_stage!r} to {observed!r}"
            )
        if observed_rank > current_rank + 1:
            raise ValueError(
                f"checkpoint id {requested[ID]!r} cannot skip from stage "
                f"{current_stage!r} to {observed!r}"
            )
        record = {
            AUDIT: requested[AUDIT],
            ID: requested[ID],
            STAGE: observed,
            STATE: requested[STATE],
        }
        _apply(path, records, record)
        processed_stage = observed

    return _NEXT_ACTIONS[processed_stage]



def _state_payload(state: dict[str, Any]) -> bytes:
    """The canonical storage bytes for a validated merge state."""
    clock, records = _storage._validated_state(state)
    return _storage._serialize(clock, records)


def _validated_paths(paths: Any) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Validate the ``checkpoint``/``state``/``audit``/``receipt`` path map."""
    if not isinstance(paths, dict):
        raise TypeError("paths must be a dict")
    if set(paths.keys()) != set(_PATH_KEYS):
        raise ValueError(
            "paths must contain exactly the keys 'checkpoint', 'state', "
            "'audit' and 'receipt'"
        )
    for key in _PATH_KEYS:
        if not isinstance(paths[key], str):
            raise TypeError(f"paths {key} must be a str")
    return {key: paths[key] for key in _PATH_KEYS}


def _validated_commit_inputs(
    paths: Any, request: Any
) -> tuple[dict[str, str], str, dict[str, Any], dict[str, str], bytes]:
    """Validate ``paths`` and a commit ``request`` before any file access.

    Returns the path map, id, the caller's state, a fresh validated event
    dict and the canonical state bytes.  The state is checked against the
    merge state contract and the event against the audit event contract,
    so their type/value errors propagate unchanged in kind.
    """
    path_map = _validated_paths(paths)
    if not isinstance(request, dict):
        raise TypeError("request must be a dict")
    if set(request.keys()) != set(_COMMIT_KEYS):
        raise ValueError(
            "request must contain exactly the keys 'id', 'state' and 'event'"
        )
    checkpoint_id = request[ID]
    if not isinstance(checkpoint_id, str):
        raise TypeError("request id must be a str")
    if _ID_RE.fullmatch(checkpoint_id) is None:
        raise ValueError("request id must match [A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}")

    payload = _state_payload(request[STATE])
    event = _audit._validated_event(request[_EVENT])

    return path_map, checkpoint_id, request[STATE], event, payload


def _planned_audit_digest(
    audit_records: list[dict[str, Any]], event: dict[str, str]
) -> str:
    """Hash the audit record the next :func:`audit.append` would write.

    Deterministic from the log's current tail: its seq is one past the
    last record and its prev is the last record's hash (or the zero hash
    for an empty log).
    """
    seq = len(audit_records) + 1
    prev = audit_records[-1][_audit.HASH] if audit_records else _audit._ZERO_HASH
    without_hash = {
        _audit.DETAIL: event[_audit.DETAIL],
        _audit.KIND: event[_audit.KIND],
        _audit.PREV: prev,
        _audit.SEQ: seq,
        _audit.SOURCE: event[_audit.SOURCE],
    }
    return _audit._record_hash(without_hash)


def _event_matches(record: dict[str, Any], event: dict[str, str]) -> bool:
    return (
        record[_audit.SOURCE] == event[_audit.SOURCE]
        and record[_audit.KIND] == event[_audit.KIND]
        and record[_audit.DETAIL] == event[_audit.DETAIL]
    )


def _advance(
    path: str,
    records: list[dict[str, str]],
    checkpoint_id: str,
    state_digest: str,
    audit_digest: str,
    stage: str,
) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    """Advance (or insert at ``prepared``) the checkpoint for one stage."""
    record = {
        AUDIT: audit_digest,
        ID: checkpoint_id,
        STAGE: stage,
        STATE: state_digest,
    }
    return _apply(path, records, record)


def _main_state_canonical_bytes(path: str) -> bytes | None:
    """Canonical complete bytes of the main state file, or ``None``.

    Only the main file is consulted: ``None`` is returned when it is
    missing or when its bytes do not decode to a valid state.  No
    exception other than a non-:class:`FileNotFoundError`
    :class:`OSError` escapes.
    """
    try:
        with open(path, "rb") as handle:
            raw = handle.read()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return None
    try:
        state = _storage._decode_state(raw)
    except _storage._DECODE_FAILURES:
        return None
    return _state_payload(state)


def _read_state_bytes(path: str) -> bytes | None:
    """Return the raw main state file bytes, or None when it is absent.

    Every :class:`OSError` other than :class:`FileNotFoundError`
    propagates unchanged.
    """
    try:
        with open(path, "rb") as handle:
            return handle.read()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return None


def _assert_state_loadable(path: str) -> None:
    """Raise unless the state is absent or a valid state survives.

    Mirrors :func:`storage.load_state`: when at least one of the main and
    backup files exists but neither holds a valid state,
    :class:`CorruptStateError` propagates unchanged; when neither file
    exists nothing happens.  Every other :class:`OSError` propagates
    unchanged as well.
    """
    try:
        _storage.load_state(path)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return


def _inspect_status(
    stage: str,
    state_matches: bool,
    audit_ok: bool,
    receipt: dict[str, str] | None,
    state_digest: str,
    audit_digest: str,
) -> str:
    """Classify one checkpoint from its stage and the S/A/R0/R1 facts.

    ``S`` is ``state_matches`` (the main state file's canonical bytes hash
    to the state digest), ``A`` is ``audit_ok`` (a valid audit chain
    carries the audit digest), ``R0`` means no receipt is bound under the
    id and ``R1`` means that receipt binds exactly both digests.
    ``prepared`` with ``not A and R0``, ``state`` with ``S and R0`` and
    ``audit`` with ``S and A and (R0 or R1)`` are recoverable;
    ``committed`` with ``S and A and R1`` is committed; everything else
    is a conflict.
    """
    r0 = receipt is None
    r1 = (
        receipt is not None
        and receipt[STATE] == state_digest
        and receipt[AUDIT] == audit_digest
    )
    if stage == PREPARED:
        if not audit_ok and r0:
            return RECOVERABLE
    elif stage == STAGE_STATE:
        if state_matches and r0:
            return RECOVERABLE
    elif stage == STAGE_AUDIT:
        if state_matches and audit_ok and (r0 or r1):
            return RECOVERABLE
    else:  # COMMITTED
        if state_matches and audit_ok and r1:
            return COMMITTED
    return CONFLICT


def inspect(paths: dict[str, str]) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    """Read-only inspection of every checkpoint against its bound artifacts.

    ``paths`` must contain exactly the str keys ``checkpoint``, ``state``,
    ``audit`` and ``receipt``, naming the checkpoint index, the main state
    file (its ``path + ".bak"`` backup is consulted for corruption
    detection, exactly as :func:`storage.load_state` does), the audit log
    and the receipt index.

    A missing checkpoint index yields ``[]`` (no other artifact is read in
    that case).  Otherwise one fresh dict per checkpoint is returned sorted
    ascending by ``id`` with the fixed key order ``audit``, ``id``,
    ``stage``, ``state``, ``status``; the first four values are copied from
    the checkpoint and ``status`` is one of ``recoverable``, ``committed``
    or ``conflict``.

    Let ``S`` mean the main state file holds a complete valid state whose
    canonical bytes hash to the state digest, ``A`` mean a valid audit
    chain contains a record whose hash is the audit digest, ``R0`` mean no
    receipt is bound under the id and ``R1`` mean that receipt binds
    exactly both digests.  A ``prepared`` checkpoint with ``not A and R0``,
    a ``state`` checkpoint with ``S and R0`` and an ``audit`` checkpoint
    with ``S and A and (R0 or R1)`` are ``recoverable``; a ``committed``
    checkpoint with ``S and A and R1`` is ``committed``; every other
    combination is ``conflict``.

    No file is created or modified.  Type violations raise
    :class:`TypeError` and a bad path key set raises :class:`ValueError`;
    when at least one of the state main/backup files exists but neither
    holds a valid state, :class:`CorruptStateError` propagates unchanged,
    as do :class:`CorruptAuditError`, :class:`CorruptReceiptError`,
    :class:`CorruptTransactionError` and :class:`OSError`.
    """
    path_map = _validated_paths(paths)

    records = _read_index(path_map[_CHECKPOINT])
    if not records:
        return []

    audit_records = _audit._read_all_records(path_map[AUDIT])
    receipts_by_id = {
        receipt[ID]: receipt for receipt in _receipt._read_index(path_map[_RECEIPT])
    }
    main_state_bytes = _main_state_canonical_bytes(path_map[STATE])
    _assert_state_loadable(path_map[STATE])

    audit_hashes = {record[_audit.HASH] for record in audit_records}

    items: list[dict[str, str]] = []
    for record in records:
        state_digest = record[STATE]
        audit_digest = record[AUDIT]
        state_matches = (
            main_state_bytes is not None
            and hashlib.sha256(main_state_bytes).hexdigest() == state_digest
        )
        audit_ok = audit_digest in audit_hashes
        receipt = receipts_by_id.get(record[ID])
        status = _inspect_status(
            record[STAGE], state_matches, audit_ok, receipt,
            state_digest, audit_digest,
        )
        items.append(
            {
                AUDIT: audit_digest,
                ID: record[ID],
                STAGE: record[STAGE],
                STATE: state_digest,
                STATUS: status,
            }
        )
    return items


def commit(paths: dict[str, str], request: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Run one replayable commit across storage, audit, receipt and checkpoint.

    ``paths`` must contain exactly the str keys ``checkpoint``, ``state``,
    ``audit`` and ``receipt``.  ``request`` must contain exactly the keys
    ``id`` (same format as :func:`checkpoint`), ``state`` (a state obeying
    the :mod:`~offline_coordination.merge` state contract) and ``event``
    (an event obeying the :mod:`~offline_coordination.audit` event
    contract).

    The state digest is the lowercase-hex SHA-256 of the complete
    canonical state bytes (including the trailing ``\\n``) that
    :mod:`~offline_coordination.storage` persists; the audit digest is
    the hash of the single audit record appended for this commit.  A
    first commit saves the state, appends exactly one audit event, binds
    a receipt carrying the id and both digests, and advances the
    checkpoint through ``prepared``, ``state``, ``audit`` and
    ``committed`` in that order.

    Replaying the same arguments -- or re-entering after an interruption
    -- resumes at the recorded stage and performs each remaining side
    effect at most once, so the result is identical and no effect is
    duplicated.  Every artifact is reconciled against the checkpoint
    stage before any file is touched: a digest conflict, or a stage
    whose state file, audit record or receipt is missing, extra or
    mismatched, raises :class:`ValueError` and leaves the files
    unchanged.

    On success a brand-new dict is returned with the key order
    ``audit``, ``id``, ``stage``, ``state`` and ``stage`` equal to
    ``committed``.  Type violations raise :class:`TypeError`; bad key
    sets, formats, state/event values, digest conflicts and stage/
    artifact mismatches raise :class:`ValueError`;
    :class:`CorruptStateError`, :class:`CorruptAuditError`,
    :class:`CorruptReceiptError`, :class:`CorruptTransactionError` and
    :class:`OSError` propagate unchanged.
    """
    (
        path_map,
        checkpoint_id,
        state,
        event,
        payload,
    ) = _validated_commit_inputs(paths, request)
    checkpoint_path = path_map[_CHECKPOINT]
    state_path = path_map[STATE]
    audit_path = path_map[AUDIT]
    receipt_path = path_map[_RECEIPT]

    state_digest = hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest()

    # Read every artifact up front.  All reconciliation below happens
    # before any mutation, so a rejected commit changes nothing.
    audit_records = _audit._read_all_records(audit_path)
    planned_audit_digest = _planned_audit_digest(audit_records, event)
    bound_receipt = _receipt.get(receipt_path, checkpoint_id)
    records = _read_index(checkpoint_path)
    existing = next(
        (record for record in records if record[ID] == checkpoint_id), None
    )
    state_on_disk = _read_state_bytes(state_path)
    # When a state file exists but neither the main file nor the backup
    # holds a valid state the situation is unrecoverable, not a digest
    # conflict: CorruptStateError propagates before any reconciliation.
    _assert_state_loadable(state_path)

    need_save = False
    need_append = False
    need_receipt = False

    if existing is None:
        # An id absent from the checkpoint index cannot have produced any
        # artifact of its own yet; a receipt bound under it is a conflict.
        if bound_receipt is not None:
            raise ValueError(
                f"receipt id {checkpoint_id!r} is already bound but no "
                "checkpoint exists for it"
            )
        audit_digest = planned_audit_digest
        stage = PREPARED
        # The state save is the first artifact effect; it is pending
        # unless the main file already holds the committed bytes.
        need_save = state_on_disk != payload
        need_append = True
        need_receipt = True
    else:
        if existing[STATE] != state_digest:
            raise ValueError(
                f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} is already bound to a "
                "different state digest"
            )
        audit_digest = existing[AUDIT]
        stage = existing[STAGE]
        audit_record = next(
            (item for item in audit_records
             if item[_audit.HASH] == audit_digest),
            None,
        )

        if stage == PREPARED:
            # The event has not been appended yet, so its record hash must
            # still be derivable from the current log tail.
            if audit_digest != planned_audit_digest:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} is already bound to a "
                    "different audit digest"
                )
            if audit_record is not None:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} is at stage 'prepared' "
                    "but its audit record is already present"
                )
            if bound_receipt is not None:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} is at stage 'prepared' "
                    "but a receipt is already bound"
                )
            # The save is pending unless the main file already holds the
            # committed bytes; save_state itself rotates any prior state.
            need_save = state_on_disk != payload
            need_append = True
            need_receipt = True
        elif stage == STAGE_STATE:
            if state_on_disk != payload:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} is past stage "
                    "'prepared' but its state file is missing or mismatched"
                )
            if bound_receipt is not None:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} is at stage 'state' but "
                    "a receipt is already bound"
                )
            if audit_record is None:
                # The append may still be pending; the log tail must still
                # derive the bound record for this event.
                if audit_digest != planned_audit_digest:
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} is at stage 'state' "
                        "but its audit record is missing"
                    )
                need_append = True
            elif not _event_matches(audit_record, event):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} audit record does not "
                    "match its committed event"
                )
            need_receipt = True
        elif stage == STAGE_AUDIT:
            if state_on_disk != payload:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} is past stage "
                    "'prepared' but its state file is missing or mismatched"
                )
            if audit_record is None:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} is past stage 'state' "
                    "but its audit record is missing"
                )
            if not _event_matches(audit_record, event):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} audit record does not "
                    "match its committed event"
                )
            if bound_receipt is None:
                need_receipt = True
            elif (
                bound_receipt[STATE] != state_digest
                or bound_receipt[AUDIT] != audit_digest
            ):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} receipt is bound to "
                    "different state or audit digests"
                )
        else:  # COMMITTED
            if state_on_disk != payload:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} is past stage "
                    "'prepared' but its state file is missing or mismatched"
                )
            if audit_record is None:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} is past stage 'state' "
                    "but its audit record is missing"
                )
            if not _event_matches(audit_record, event):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} audit record does not "
                    "match its committed event"
                )
            if bound_receipt is None:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} is committed but its "
                    "receipt is missing"
                )
            if (
                bound_receipt[STATE] != state_digest
                or bound_receipt[AUDIT] != audit_digest
            ):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} receipt is bound to "
                    "different state or audit digests"
                )

    # Reconciliation succeeded; perform each remaining effect at most
    # once and advance the checkpoint after every durable step.
    if existing is None:
        records = _advance(
            checkpoint_path, records, checkpoint_id,
            state_digest, audit_digest, PREPARED,
        )

    if stage == PREPARED:
        if need_save:
            _storage.save_state(state_path, state)
        records = _advance(
            checkpoint_path, records, checkpoint_id,
            state_digest, audit_digest, STAGE_STATE,
        )
        stage = STAGE_STATE

    if stage == STAGE_STATE:
        if need_append:
            _audit.append(audit_path, event)
        records = _advance(
            checkpoint_path, records, checkpoint_id,
            state_digest, audit_digest, STAGE_AUDIT,
        )
        stage = STAGE_AUDIT

    if stage == STAGE_AUDIT:
        if need_receipt:
            _receipt.put(
                receipt_path,
                {AUDIT: audit_digest, ID: checkpoint_id, STATE: state_digest},
            )
        _advance(
            checkpoint_path, records, checkpoint_id,
            state_digest, audit_digest, COMMITTED,
        )

    return {
        AUDIT: audit_digest,
        ID: checkpoint_id,
        STAGE: COMMITTED,
        STATE: state_digest,
    }

1	"""Read-only audit replication batches.
2	
3	A batch is a single UTF-8 compact JSON object (non-ASCII preserved, no
4	whitespace) terminated by exactly one ``\\n``::
5	
6	    {"after":...,"complete":...,"next":...,"records":[...],"version":1}
7	
8	The top-level keys are fixed in the order ``after``, ``complete``,
9	``next``, ``records``, ``version`` and ``version`` is always the integer
10	1.  ``after`` echoes the request's ``after`` argument.  ``records`` holds
11	up to ``limit`` (at most 1000) audit records whose ``seq`` is greater
12	than ``after``, in audit order, each preserving the audit record key
13	order ``detail, hash, kind, prev, seq, source`` and its original values.
14	``next`` is the seq of the last record in the batch, or ``after`` itself
15	when the batch is empty; ``complete`` is true when no record follows the
16	batch, and an empty ``records`` list is only valid when ``complete`` is
17	true.  Batches are generated solely through :func:`audit.read`, so the
18	audit log is never modified and :class:`~offline_coordination.audit.
19	CorruptAuditError` and :class:`OSError` propagate unchanged.
20	
21	:func:`import_batch` validates a batch against this byte contract and
22	appends its records to the local log.  It returns a dict with the fixed
23	key order ``need``, ``next``, ``status``.  When the batch starts beyond
24	the local log (``after`` greater than the local last seq ``L``) nothing is
25	written and ``status`` is ``"missing"`` with ``need`` holding the gap
26	``[L + 1, after]`` and ``next`` set to ``L``.  Otherwise records already
27	present locally must match field by field (a mismatch raises
28	:class:`ValueError`); the matching prefix is skipped idempotently and
29	only the contiguous suffix past ``L`` is appended, linked to the local
30	last hash.  ``need`` is then ``None``, ``next`` is ``max(L, batch.next)``
31	and ``status`` is ``"applied"`` when records were appended, else
32	``"duplicate"``.  Any failure leaves the log untouched.
33	
34	Batches are checked only against the byte contract: canonical encoding, key
35	order, the seq/prev/hash chain and the stored values.  Value-domain rules
36	enforced by :func:`audit.append` on event input (the kind enum, non-empty
37	string fields) are *not* re-enforced here, so every log :func:`audit.read`
38	accepts round-trips through :func:`export_batch`/:func:`import_batch`.  The
39	append itself is atomic: when the write, flush or fsync step raises
40	:class:`OSError` the error propagates unchanged and the log is left
41	byte-identical to its pre-call state (still missing when it was missing).
42	
43	:func:`apply_remote` persists remote state applications in a version-1
44	*ledger*: one UTF-8 compact JSON object (keys sorted lexicographically,
45	exactly one trailing ``\\n``) with the top-level keys ``audit``,
46	``requests``, ``state`` and ``version`` (``version`` is the integer 1).
47	``state`` holds the current :mod:`~offline_coordination.merge` state,
48	``requests`` binds each accepted request id to the digest of its request,
49	and ``audit`` lists one entry per successful application in order; each
50	entry carries ``after``/``before`` state digests, the request ``id`` and
51	``source`` and a contiguous ``seq`` starting at 1, every entry after the
52	first chaining its ``before`` to the previous entry's ``after`` and the
53	last ``after`` hashing the stored state.  A missing ledger stands for the
54	request's ``base`` state with empty indexes; any existing file that fails
55	the byte, structure, state or index rules is rejected with
56	:class:`ValueError` and left untouched.
57	
58	Replaying a request whose ``id`` is already bound to exactly the same
59	request digest always yields ``duplicate`` from the saved binding alone,
60	immediately or after other commits: one item per remote record in
61	ascending key order, each already duplicate with an empty ``need`` map,
62	and no receipt; the ledger is never read for modification on a replay.
63	A bound ``id`` presented with a different request raises
64	:class:`ValueError`.  Every successful commit is one durable transaction:
65	write, flush, file sync, replacement and directory sync all lie inside
66	its boundary, and an :class:`OSError` at any stage propagates unchanged
67	with the file system restored to its pre-call state.
68	
69	Each commit is additionally backed by a *recovery intent* so a crash of
70	the committing process itself can be reconciled later, across processes.
71	Before anything is replaced, the commit publishes an intent at ``path +
72	".txn"``: one UTF-8 compact JSON object (keys recursively sorted,
73	exactly one trailing ``\n``) recording only ``version`` (the integer 1),
74	``phase``, the lowercase hex SHA-256 digests of the new and old ledger
75	bytes (``newDigest``/``oldDigest``) and the safe base names of the
76	candidate and predecessor transaction files, all confined to the
77	ledger's own directory; when the ledger did not exist, ``oldDigest`` and
78	``predecessor`` are both ``null``.  The intent starts in phase
79	``prepared`` and is republished as ``installed`` only after the new
80	ledger has replaced the old one and the directory has synced; the
81	intent's own creation and phase change each sync the file and the
82	directory.  A crash before the ``installed`` intent is durable leaves
83	the commit unconfirmed: :func:`recover_ledger` keeps or restores the old
84	bytes (byte-for-byte, and missing again when the path was missing) and
85	deletes the referenced candidate.  A crash afterwards lets
86	:func:`recover_ledger` verify the new bytes against ``newDigest`` and
87	finish the cleanup.  Only files the intent references are removed, the
88	intent itself is deleted last and the directory is synced, and a
89	repeated call reports ``clean`` without scanning random artifacts.
90	
91	:func:`recover_ledger` returns a fresh dict with the key order
92	``digest``, ``status``: ``clean`` when no intent exists, ``rolled-back``
93	or ``completed`` after a recovery, with ``digest`` holding the digest of
94	the resulting ledger bytes (``None`` when the path is missing).  A
95	``path`` that is not a str raises :class:`TypeError`; an intent that
96	fails to parse, or whose fields, phase, names, digests or necessary
97	artifacts are invalid, raises :class:`CorruptRecoveryError` (a
98	:class:`ValueError`) without touching the ledger or any unrelated file;
99	an :class:`OSError` while reading, replacing, deleting or syncing
100	propagates unchanged with enough intent and artifacts left for a retry.
101	The ledger write entry points run this recovery automatically after
102	their input validation, before the ledger is read.
103	
104	:func:`inspect_recovery` diagnoses an explicit, non-empty list of ledger
105	paths without modifying anything: only each listed ledger, its intent
106	and the artifacts the intent references are read.  Each report carries
107	``path``, ``status``, ``phase``, ``digest``, ``artifacts``, ``action``
108	and ``error`` -- ``clean`` with a null phase and action when no intent
109	exists (the digest still summarizes the ledger bytes, or is null when
110	the path is missing), ``pending`` with the intent's phase and the
111	suggested action (``rollback``/``complete``) plus the candidate and
112	predecessor existence, digest match and completeness when an intent is
113	valid, ``blocked``/``corrupt`` when the intent or a necessary artifact
114	is invalid, and ``failed``/``os-error`` when reading fails.
115	:func:`recover_many` is the controlled batch form of
116	:func:`recover_ledger` over the same kind of list: every path is
117	recovered in order, one ledger's failure never stops or rolls back the
118	others, a :class:`CorruptRecoveryError` becomes a ``blocked``/``corrupt``
119	item and an :class:`OSError` a ``failed``/``os-error`` item, and failed
120	ledgers keep their intent and artifacts so a re-run retries them
121	independently.  Both validate the whole list (a non-empty list of
122	non-empty, distinct strings) before any file is read or modified.
123	
124	:func:`apply_signed_remote` adds an offline-verifiable authentication
125	boundary in front of the same application flow.  It receives the ledger
126	path, a keyring, an envelope and the current moment.  The envelope
127	carries exactly ``node``, ``keyVersion``, ``request`` and ``signature``;
128	the request follows the :func:`apply_remote` contract and its ``source``
129	must equal the envelope's ``node``.  The keyring maps node names to
130	credential entries, each holding exactly ``version`` (a positive integer,
131	unique per node), ``secret`` (64 lowercase hex characters decoding to the
132	32-byte HMAC key), ``notBefore``/``notAfter`` (non-negative integers
133	bounding the validity period, both bounds inclusive) and ``revoked``.
134	The signed payload is the canonical compact UTF-8 JSON encoding of
135	``node``, ``keyVersion`` and ``request`` with every object key
136	recursively sorted lexicographically and non-ASCII preserved; the
137	signature is the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 computed with the selected key
138	and compared in constant time.  Keys are selected by exact node and
139	version with no fallback: unknown credentials, a revoked, not-yet-valid
140	or expired key, a source/node identity mismatch and a signature mismatch
141	all raise :class:`AuthenticationError` (a :class:`ValueError`) before the
142	ledger is ever read, so a failed verification creates no file.  Replays
143	are authenticated against the *current* keyring, so a later revocation or
144	expiry cannot be bypassed through a historical request binding.  Audit
145	entries committed through :func:`apply_signed_remote` record the verified
146	credentials under ``auth``; entries without ``auth`` remain readable and
147	:func:`apply_remote` keeps its public behaviour and ledger format.
148	
149	:func:`export_proof` and :func:`verify_proof` add offline audit-proof
150	exchange over the same ledger.  A proof is one version-1 UTF-8 compact
151	JSON object -- every object key recursively sorted lexicographically,
152	non-ASCII preserved, exactly one trailing ``\\n`` -- with the top-level
153	keys ``digest``, ``endSeq``, ``entries``, ``firstBefore``, ``lastAfter``,
154	``startSeq`` and ``version``.  ``startSeq``/``endSeq`` name the covered
155	audit range, ``firstBefore`` is the state digest before the first covered
156	entry and ``lastAfter`` the state digest after the last one; ``entries``
157	hold the ledger entries in range unchanged, each carrying ``after``/
158	``before`` state digests, ``id``, ``seq`` and ``source`` with the optional
159	``auth`` binding.  ``digest`` is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the compact
160	canonical encoding (with no trailing newline) of the proof object with
161	the ``digest`` key itself removed.  :func:`verify_proof` is purely
162	offline: it reads neither the ledger nor the keyring.
163	
164	:func:`compare_proofs` relates two proofs offline, on top of that same
165	purely local verification.  Both arguments are :class:`bytes`; they are
166	first independently checked against the exact :func:`verify_proof`
167	contract, so a non-bytes argument raises :class:`TypeError` and either
168	proof being invalid raises :class:`InvalidProofError` before any
169	comparison.  The ledger, the keyring and the filesystem are never read
170	and neither input is modified.  The result is one version-1 UTF-8
171	compact JSON object -- every object key sorted lexicographically,
172	non-ASCII preserved, exactly one trailing ``\\n`` -- with the fixed
173	top-level keys ``common``, ``conflictSeq``, ``left``, ``overlap``,
174	``relation``, ``right`` and ``version`` (``version`` is the integer 1).
175	``left``/``right`` each carry the proof ``digest`` and its
176	``startSeq``/``endSeq``.  ``overlap`` is the closed shared seq interval
177	``[start, end]`` or ``null`` when the two ranges are disjoint; disjoint
178	ranges never raise and keep both sides' ranges.  With an overlap, the
179	complete entries at every shared seq are compared in ascending seq
180	order -- boundary and proof digests alone are never enough.  If every
181	shared entry matches, ``relation`` is ``"same"`` (identical ranges),
182	``"left-prefix"``/``"right-prefix"`` (same start and the shorter side
183	matches in full, named for the shorter side) or ``"overlap"``
184	otherwise; ``common`` then names the last shared boundary as
185	``{"after", "seq"}`` -- the last common entry's seq and after digest.
186	The first shared seq whose complete entry differs makes ``relation``
187	``"fork"`` with ``conflictSeq`` that earliest seq (never skipped past);
188	``common`` is the last equal entry when an equal entry precedes it, the
189	prior boundary ``{"after", "seq"}`` when the first shared entry already
190	conflicts but its ``before`` digests agree (its seq may be 0), and
191	``null`` when those ``before`` digests differ.  ``conflictSeq`` is
192	``null`` for every non-fork relation.  The bytes are deterministic for
193	equal inputs; swapping the inputs only exchanges ``left``/``right`` and
194	mirrors the prefix direction.
195	
196	:func:`plan_merge` turns that read-only comparison into a read-only merge
197	plan.  It takes both proof byte strings and a conflict ``policy`` --
198	``"left"``, ``"right"`` or ``"manual"``; any other value raises
199	:class:`ValueError` -- and validates every argument type before parsing
200	either proof, so a malformed proof never masks a :class:`TypeError` and an
201	invalid proof still raises :class:`InvalidProofError`.  Disjoint ranges,
202	or a fork whose common boundary cannot be confirmed, raise
203	:class:`ValueError` instead of producing a speculative plan.  Only
204	complete entries strictly after the common boundary become steps: an
205	unforked history accepts the longer side's tail as an ``extension``; a
206	fork accepts the selected side's tail (``selected``) and rejects the
207	other (``rejected``), while ``manual`` marks both tails ``manual`` and
208	references them from ``unresolved``.  The plan is one version-1 UTF-8
209	compact JSON object -- keys recursively sorted, non-ASCII preserved,
210	exactly one trailing ``\\n`` -- with the top-level keys ``common``,
211	``left``, ``policy``, ``relation``, ``right``, ``steps``, ``unresolved``
212	and ``version``; steps carry the original entries unchanged and are
213	ordered by ascending seq with the left side first on ties.  The plan is
214	byte-stable for equal inputs, mirrors left/right when the proofs are
215	swapped together with a ``left``/``right`` policy, and never touches the
216	filesystem or the inputs.
217	
218	:func:`resolve_merge` closes a ``manual`` plan read-only.  It takes the
219	plan byte string, the same two proofs and a list of decisions; only a
220	``manual`` plan produced by :func:`plan_merge` for exactly those proofs
221	may be resolved -- a plan from any other policy is a structurally valid
222	version-1 plan whose steps differ from the regenerated manual plan and
223	is therefore rejected as stale before any decision is considered.
224	A structurally invalid plan (encoding, duplicate keys, version-1
225	structure) raises :class:`InvalidPlanError`; a structurally valid plan
226	that is not byte-for-byte the manual plan regenerated from the proofs
227	(digest, relation, common boundary, side summaries, steps or unresolved
228	references) raises :class:`StalePlanError`; both are
229	:class:`ValueError` subclasses.  Each decision carries only ``side``,
230	``seq`` and ``action`` (``"accept"`` or ``"reject"``), resolving one
231	unresolved reference; missing, duplicate, extra or out-of-range
232	references and illegal choices raise :class:`InvalidResolutionError`
233	(a :class:`ValueError`).  Accepted entries must chain contiguously from
234	the common boundary -- at most one accepted side per seq, no acceptance
235	past a rejected seq, an unbroken seq and digest chain.  The result is
236	one version-1 compact JSON object with the top-level keys ``common``,
237	``left``, ``planDigest``, ``relation``, ``right``, ``steps``,
238	``unresolved`` and ``version``; manual steps become
239	``accept``/``reject`` with the fixed reasons ``manual-accepted``/
240	``manual-rejected``, non-manual steps, carried audit entries and ``auth``
241	bindings are unchanged, ``unresolved`` is empty and ``planDigest`` is the
242	lowercase hex SHA-256 of the complete source plan bytes.  Resolution is
243	deterministic, mirrors under a left/right swap with matching decisions,
244	and never touches the filesystem or the inputs.
245	
246	:func:`commit_resolution` is the write entry point that lands a manual
247	resolution in the ledger.  It takes the ledger path, the canonical
248	resolution bytes, the original plan bytes, both proofs and the landing
249	material -- the final ``state`` plus ``requests`` binding every accepted
250	entry id to its request digest.  Both proofs are verified offline and
251	the plan and resolution are checked against the freshly regenerated
252	manual plan (:class:`StalePlanError` otherwise, without touching the
253	ledger); the ledger itself must still sit at the resolution's common
254	boundary (:class:`StaleLedgerError`, a :class:`ValueError`).  A fully
255	identical replay is recognized before that staleness check and returns
256	``duplicate``; a resolution accepting nothing returns ``unchanged`` and
257	writes nothing.  Otherwise the final state, the request bindings and
258	the contiguous accepted entries -- rejected entries never enter the
259	audit -- are written in one fail-safe replacement, returning
260	``applied``.  The result carries only ``next``, ``resolutionDigest``
261	and ``status``.
262	
263	:func:`recover_authorized` puts an offline-verifiable authorization
264	boundary and a durable operation audit around the same batch recovery.
265	It takes the ledger path list, a keyring, a ticket, the current moment
266	and the recovery audit path.  The ticket is one UTF-8 compact JSON
267	object -- every object key recursively sorted lexicographically,
268	non-ASCII preserved, no trailing newline or any other trailing byte --
269	carrying exactly ``payload`` and ``signature``.  The payload holds exactly ``issuer``,
270	``keyVersion``, ``nonce``, ``notBefore``, ``notAfter`` and the ordered
271	``paths``; the signature is the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of the
272	canonical compact payload encoding, computed with the key the keyring
273	binds to the exact issuer and version (the
274	:func:`apply_signed_remote` keyring rules) and compared in constant
275	time.  The command paths must equal the ticket paths item for item --
276	never expanded, reordered or implicitly normalized.  Unknown
277	credentials, a revoked, not-yet-valid or expired key or ticket, a path
278	mismatch and a signature mismatch all raise :class:`AuthenticationError`
279	before any ledger is read, so a failed authorization creates no audit
280	record, consumes no nonce and leaves no temporary file.  Type faults in
281	the arguments raise :class:`TypeError` (a :class:`bool` never poses as
282	``moment``); a malformed ticket key set, nonce, validity interval,
283	encoding or signature format raises :class:`ValueError`.
284	
285	Once authorized, the batch runs in the :func:`recover_many` order with
286	the same per-ledger isolation and the same public item structure, and
287	every step is recorded in an append-only recovery audit at the given
288	path: a canonical JSONL hash chain (recursively sorted keys, one
289	trailing ``\\n`` per record, each record chaining the previous record's
290	SHA-256) where every record is written, flushed and synced before the
291	step it gates.  The first use of a nonce persists a ``batch`` header
292	binding the ticket digest, the issuer and the ordered paths; each
293	ledger then gets a ``before`` record (original digest, recovery phase,
294	planned action) and an ``after`` record (new digest, status, failure
295	category).  An :class:`OSError` while reading the audit or writing,
296	flushing or syncing a record propagates unchanged and leaves a
297	consistent, retryable chain prefix.  Re-entering with the same nonce
298	and the same ticket reuses the recorded results and only continues the
299	paths not yet settled; a process interrupted after a recovery but
300	before its result record is completed from the recorded action and
301	digests, without repeating side effects.  The same nonce bound to a
302	different ticket raises :class:`ReplayError` (a :class:`ValueError`)
303	without modifying any file, and a corrupt chain raises
304	:class:`CorruptRecoveryAuditError` (a :class:`ValueError`).
305	
306	:func:`export_recovery_audit` pages the recovery audit read-only:
307	``after``/``limit`` select the window, the whole chain is validated
308	and a missing audit is treated as an empty chain.
309	
310	:func:`export_recovery_checkpoint` adds an offline signature anchor
311	over the same chain.  It takes the audit path, a keyring, an issuer,
312	a key version and a moment, reads and validates the whole chain
313	read-only and returns one canonical compact UTF-8 JSON object -- keys
314	recursively sorted, non-ASCII preserved, no trailing newline or any
315	other trailing byte -- carrying exactly ``payload`` and ``signature``.
316	The payload binds exactly ``issuer``, ``keyVersion``, ``lastSeq``,
317	``moment``, ``tail`` and ``version`` (the integer 1); ``lastSeq`` is
318	the chain's last seq (0 for a missing audit) and ``tail`` the last
319	record hash (the zero hash for an empty chain).  The signature is the
320	lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of the canonical compact payload bytes under
321	the key the keyring binds to the exact issuer and version, with no
322	fallback; unknown credentials and a revoked, not-yet-valid or expired
323	key raise :class:`AuthenticationError`, a corrupt chain raises
324	:class:`CorruptRecoveryAuditError` and an :class:`OSError` while
325	reading propagates unchanged.
326	
327	:func:`verify_recovery_page` verifies a paging dict against such a
328	checkpoint entirely offline: it reads no file.  The checkpoint is
329	parsed and its HMAC is verified against the current keyring (exact
330	issuer/version, usable at the given moment, so a later revocation or
331	expiry rejects the checkpoint as it does a replay); the moment bound
332	into the payload is part of the signed anchor itself and needs no
333	equality with the verification time.  The first round passes no cursor
334	and the page's ``after`` must be zero; every later round passes the
335	``{"digest", "next", "tail"}`` cursor built from the previous result,
336	requiring ``after`` to equal the cursor's ``next``, the first record
337	to chain to the cursor's ``tail`` and the cursor ``digest`` to equal
338	this checkpoint's SHA-256 digest, so a cursor can never resume
339	another checkpoint.  Every page's records must be contiguous from
340	``after + 1`` (no gap, reordering or duplicate), hash-correct and
341	chained inside the page and across its boundaries, and verification
342	never crosses the signed ``lastSeq``; before that seq an empty page
343	or a wrong ``complete`` flag is rejected as an invalid page.  The
344	result carries the fixed keys ``digest``, ``lastSeq``, ``status`` and
345	``tail``: reaching the signed tail yields ``"verified"``, every
346	earlier page ``"continue"``.  An empty checkpoint accepts only an
347	empty page starting at zero and reports seq 0, the zero hash and
348	``"verified"``.  Type faults raise :class:`TypeError` (a bool never
349	poses as an int), keyring faults raise :class:`ValueError`,
350	checkpoint faults raise :class:`InvalidRecoveryCheckpointError` and
351	page or cursor faults raise :class:`InvalidRecoveryPageError`; both
352	format errors subclass :class:`ValueError`.  No input or file is
353	modified.
354	
355	:func:`verify_recovery_checkpoints` verifies a whole batch of
356	checkpoints offline, in input order, and never reads a file.  Each
357	item carries exactly a non-empty, batch-unique ``id``, the
358	``checkpoint`` bytes and the ordered, non-empty ``pages`` exported
359	for that checkpoint; the batch is validated in full before any item
360	is verified, so a container, field or element type fault raises
361	:class:`TypeError` and an empty list, an empty or duplicate id or an
362	empty page list raises :class:`ValueError` without producing any
363	result.  Every item is then verified in isolation from a zero cursor
364	through the exact :func:`verify_recovery_page` paging rules, each
365	round resuming from a cursor bound to the same checkpoint digest and
366	the previous page's chain tail, and one item's failure never stops
367	the later items.  Each checkpoint selects its key by its own exact
368	issuer and version with no fallback, so checkpoints signed before
369	and after a key rotation verify independently in the same batch as
370	long as the keyring retains both versions.  An item that reaches the
371	signed ``lastSeq`` must have no further pages; an item whose pages
372	run out earlier is ``incomplete`` and keeps its verified boundary.
373	Every item reports ``id``, the checkpoint ``digest``, the signed
374	``issuer`` and ``keyVersion`` (both ``None`` when the checkpoint
375	does not parse), the verified ``boundary`` (``None`` when nothing
376	was verified), a ``status`` of ``verified``, ``incomplete``,
377	``invalid-checkpoint``, ``invalid-page`` or ``unauthenticated`` and
378	an ``error`` (``None`` exactly when the item verified).  The result
379	is a fresh dict with the fixed key order ``items``, ``version``
380	(the integer 1); only batch-level or keyring-level faults raise,
381	never one item's verification failure.
382	
383	:func:`adjudicate_recovery` turns those per-site verification results
384	into one offline aggregate verdict, still reading no file.  It takes a
385	non-empty ``items`` list, a ``policy``, a ``keyring`` and ``moment``.
386	Each item contains exactly a non-empty, batch-unique ``id`` and
387	``attestation`` bytes -- one canonical compact UTF-8 JSON object with
388	recursively sorted keys, non-ASCII preserved and no trailing newline
389	or any other trailing byte, carrying exactly ``payload`` and
390	``signature``.  The payload binds exactly ``batch``, ``site``,
391	``keyVersion`` and ``result`` with no extra fields; ``result`` follows
392	the public single-item :func:`verify_recovery_checkpoints` report
393	shape (``boundary``, ``digest``, ``error``, ``id``, ``issuer``,
394	``keyVersion``, ``status``).  Every legal single-item result is
395	accepted: a ``verified`` result always carries the checkpoint
396	identity, positive key version and signed boundary, while a
397	non-verified result may carry null ``issuer``/``keyVersion`` (when the
398	checkpoint did not parse) or a null boundary -- its identity, digest,
399	boundary and status are preserved on the report -- and only a
400	``verified`` result may count.
