cat >> README.md <<'MDEOF'

## Pruning multi-round convergence archives

`plan_chain_prune(paths, checkpoint, decision, policy, keyring, moment)` builds a read-only signed plan for trimming persisted convergence archives, reading the archive files but never modifying, creating or deleting them. `paths` is an explicit, non-empty list of distinct file paths; each archive is one version-1 canonical JSON object (recursively sorted keys, non-ASCII preserved, exactly one trailing `\n`) carrying exactly `project` (a unique non-empty identifier), `certificate` and the ordered `rounds` (each `{confirmation, seq}`, numbered consecutively from one), with the certificate and every confirmation carried as non-empty lowercase hex bytes. The sealing `checkpoint` is a `seal_chain_checkpoint` packet authenticated against the current keyring through the exact `verify_chain_suffix` rules (exact issuer/version, usable at `moment`, no fallback). An archive is eligible for pruning only when its certificate digest is part of the checkpoint's pruned evidence prefix and its whole round group re-verifies through the exact `verify_fork_convergence` rules against `decision`, `policy` and `keyring` at `moment`; non-eligible archives are retained and when nothing is eligible a `ValueError` is raised. The result is one canonical compact `{payload, signature}` object with no trailing byte; the payload binds exactly `checkpoint` (its SHA-256), `delete` (eligible projects ascending), `retain` (the SHA-256 of every retained archive's bytes, ascending), `source` and `target` (each a map from an eligible project to the digest of its archive bytes before pruning and of its trimmed project-marker archive afterwards) and `version` (integer 1). It carries no moment or project identifier of its own and is signed with the checkpoint's own exact issuer/key, so equal arguments produce byte-identical plans. Container/field type faults raise `TypeError` (a bool never poses as an int); an empty/duplicate path or project, a wrong key set or an illegal version raises `ValueError`; a missing archive raises `FileNotFoundError`; an illegal archive or checkpoint raises `InvalidPruneError`; credential and signature faults raise `AuthenticationError`.

`prune_chain_archives(items, keyring)` executes the plans in one controlled batch. Each item holds exactly a unique non-empty `id`, an archive `path`, the signed `plan`, the sealing `checkpoint` and a `header` naming the exact signing `issuer`/`keyVersion` (the checkpoint sealer) and the non-negative prune `moment`; the batch structure and keyring are validated first. Each item then runs in strict input order and full isolation: bad credentials, malformed plans or checkpoints and stale archives are recorded for that item alone, the archive is left unchanged and the batch continues. When the archive at `path` hashes to the plan's source digest for its project, the planned trimmed target (one canonical `{project, version}` marker ending in one `\n`, the certificate and all round bytes gone) is installed in a crash-safe two-phase transaction, and the receipt status is `pruned`; when the archive already hashes to the target digest nothing is written and the status is `duplicate`; any other content records `StalePruneError`. An `OSError` raised while writing, flushing, syncing a file or directory, replacing or deleting is recorded for that item with its original text and leaves the retryable transaction material in place. The transaction uses only same-directory files — a unique candidate, the hard-linked predecessor and the `path + ".prune.txn"` intent — whose only phases are `prepared` and `installed`; unrelated files are never scanned or touched. The batch returns, in input order, fresh dicts keyed `id`, `receipt` and `error`. The receipt is one canonical compact `{payload, signature}` object binding the `status`, the complete plan, the `checkpoint` digest, `beforeDigest`/`afterDigest` (equal for a duplicate), the full `delete` and `retain` digests, the prune `moment` and `version` 1, signed under the exact header key. The first completion and a same-plan re-entry (an interrupted transaction whose `.prune.txn` intent is still present) return one identical signed receipt: an installed same-plan intent is completed to the original `pruned` receipt and a prepared one is rolled back and retried.

`recover_chain_prune(path)` settles one interrupted prune transaction, touching only the files its `path + ".prune.txn"` intent names. With no intent it returns `clean` without scanning artifacts, with the current archive digest (or `None` when the path is missing). A `prepared` intent rolls the source bytes back byte-for-byte from the retained predecessor (the path is removed again when it did not exist) and deletes the candidate, reporting `rolled-back`; an `installed` intent requires the current bytes to hash to `newDigest`, removes the remaining artifacts and reports `completed`; the intent is deleted last and the directory synced so a repeat returns `clean`, and every result carries the resulting digest. A non-str path raises `TypeError`; a malformed intent (wrong key set, version, phase, target, name confinement or digest binding, or a missing necessary artifact) raises `InvalidPruneError` without touching unrelated files; an `OSError` while reading, replacing, deleting or syncing propagates unchanged with the intent and artifacts retained for a retry. `InvalidPruneError` and `StalePruneError` both subclass `ValueError`. Planning and recovery read files but planning changes nothing; the existing checkpoint continuation verification, replacement chains, module commands and README command surface are unchanged.
MDEOF

The plan is parsed structurally, bound to the item checkpoint and
    authenticated, and the checkpoint is parsed and authenticated
    against the exact header issuer/version (which must name the
    checkpoint's own sealer), usable at the header moment with no
    fallback.  Structural faults raise :class:`InvalidPruneError`;
    credential faults raise :class:`AuthenticationError`.
    """
    plan_raw = item[PRUNE_PLAN]
    checkpoint = item[PRUNE_CHECKPOINT]
    header = item[PRUNE_HEADER]
    issuer = header[VD_ISSUER]
    key_version = header[KEY_VERSION]
    moment = header[PRUNE_MOMENT]

    plan_payload, plan_signature, plan_envelope = _prune_parse_plan(plan_raw)
    checkpoint_digest = hashlib.sha256(checkpoint).hexdigest()
    if plan_payload[PRUNE_CHECKPOINT] != checkpoint_digest:
        raise _prune_invalid("the plan is not bound to the item checkpoint")
    try:
        cp_payload, cp_signature = _parse_chain_checkpoint(checkpoint)
    except InvalidCheckpointError as exc:
        raise _prune_invalid(str(exc)) from exc
    if cp_payload[VD_ISSUER] != issuer or cp_payload[KEY_VERSION] != key_version:
        raise AuthenticationError(
            "the prune header must name the exact checkpoint sealer issuer "
            "and key version"
        )
    entry = _usable_checkpoint_key(
        validated_keyring, issuer, key_version, moment
    )
    secret = entry[SECRET]
    cp_expected = hmac.new(
        bytes.fromhex(secret),
        _checkpoint_compact(cp_payload),
        hashlib.sha256,
    ).hexdigest()
    if not hmac.compare_digest(cp_expected, cp_signature):
        raise AuthenticationError(
            "chain checkpoint signature does not match"
        )
    plan_expected = hmac.new(
        bytes.fromhex(secret),
        _prune_compact(plan_payload),
        hashlib.sha256,
    ).hexdigest()
    if not hmac.compare_digest(plan_expected, plan_signature):
        raise AuthenticationError("prune plan signature does not match")
    return {
        "plan_payload": plan_payload,
        "plan_envelope": plan_envelope,
        "checkpoint_digest": checkpoint_digest,
        "plan_digest": hashlib.sha256(plan_raw).hexdigest(),
        "secret": secret,
    }


def _prune_build_receipt(
    item: dict,
    prepared: dict,
    project: str,
    status: str,
) -> bytes:
    """Build and self-validate the canonical signed receipt for one item.

    Binds the status, the complete plan envelope, the checkpoint
    digest, the before/after archive digests, the full delete and
    retain digests, the header moment and version 1.  It is a pure
    function of the item and outcome, so the first completion and a
    same-plan re-entry yield byte-identical receipts.
    """
    plan_payload = prepared["plan_payload"]
    moment = item[PRUNE_HEADER][PRUNE_MOMENT]
    if status == PRUNE_STATUS_DUPLICATE:
        # Nothing changed: the observed before state already is the
        # target state, so both digests bind the target bytes.
        before_digest = after_digest = plan_payload[PRUNE_TARGET][project]
    else:
        before_digest = plan_payload[PRUNE_SOURCE][project]
        after_digest = plan_payload[PRUNE_TARGET][project]
    payload = {
        PRUNE_AFTER: after_digest,
        PRUNE_BEFORE: before_digest,
        PRUNE_CHECKPOINT: prepared["checkpoint_digest"],
        PRUNE_DELETE: list(plan_payload[PRUNE_DELETE]),
        PRUNE_MOMENT: moment,
        PRUNE_PLAN: prepared["plan_envelope"],
        PRUNE_RETAIN: list(plan_payload[PRUNE_RETAIN]),
        PRUNE_STATUS: status,
        VERSION: CHAIN_PRUNE_VERSION,
    }
    signature = hmac.new(
        bytes.fromhex(prepared["secret"]),
        _prune_compact(payload),
        hashlib.sha256,
    ).hexdigest()
    receipt = _prune_compact(
        {TICKET_PAYLOAD: payload, SIGNATURE: signature}
    )
    # Self-check: every receipt this module hands out must itself
    # satisfy the receipt contract and its HMAC and bindings.

content.text:
Done. The baseline had the adjudication chain checkpoint (`seal_chain_checkpoint`) and suffix verification but no convergence-certificate/round archive trimming. I added the complete prune layer to `offline_coordination/replication.py` (+1354 lines), documented it in `README.md`, and added `tests/test_chain_prune.py` (52 tests; full suite 1385 passing).

## What was added

**`plan_chain_prune(paths, checkpoint, decision, policy, keyring, moment)`** — read-only signed plan
- Parses version-1 canonical archives (recursively sorted compact UTF-8 JSON, non-ASCII unescaped, one trailing `\n`) carrying exactly `project`, `certificate` and ordered `rounds` (`{confirmation, seq}` from 1), bytes as lowercase hex.
- Authenticates the sealing checkpoint through the existing `verify_chain_suffix` rules; an archive is eligible only when its certificate digest is in the checkpoint's evidence prefix **and** its whole round group re-verifies via `verify_fork_convergence`. No eligible project → `ValueError`.
- Returns a canonical `{payload, signature}` (no trailing byte) binding `checkpoint`, ascending `delete`, ascending `retain`, per-project `source`/`target` digests and `version: 1`, HMAC-signed with the checkpoint's own exact issuer/key; byte-stable for equal args; changes no file.

**`prune_chain_archives(items, keyring)`** — controlled batch
- Items hold exactly `id`, `path`, `plan`, `checkpoint` and a `header` (`issuer`/`keyVersion`/`moment`). Batch shape and keyring validated first; each item then runs in full isolation — bad credentials, malformed plans/checkpoints, and stale archives are recorded (`id`/`receipt`/`error`) with the archive untouched while later items continue.
- Source match → two-phase crash-safe install of the trimmed `{project, version}` marker (`pruned` receipt); target match → `duplicate`; otherwise `StalePruneError`. Uses only same-directory unique candidate, hard-linked predecessor and `.prune.txn` intent (phases `prepared`/`installed` only); `OSError` propagates into the item record with retryable material preserved.
- Same-plan in-flight re-entry returns the identical `pruned` receipt (installed intent completed; prepared rolled back and retried).

**`recover_chain_prune(path)`** — `clean`/`rolled-back`/`completed` with digest; touches only intent-named files; corrupt intent → `InvalidPruneError`; `OSError` propagates unchanged.

**Errors:** `InvalidPruneError` and `StalePruneError(both ValueError subclasses); TypeError/ValueError classification with bool≠int throughout.

Existing checkpoint continuation, replacement chains, module commands and all prior behavior are unchanged; no new CLI entry point was added.
